title: Cloud Types
description: The principal cloud genera classified by altitude and appearance.

results.name: Cirrus
results.description: Thin, wispy strands of ice crystals often called mare's tails.

results.name: Cirrocumulus
results.description: Small white patches or ripples of cloud, forming a mackerel sky.

results.name: Cirrostratus
results.description: Transparent, whitish veil that can produce a halo around the sun or moon.

results.name: Altocumulus
results.description: White or grey layers of rounded masses, often in groups or waves.

results.name: Altostratus
results.description: Grey or blue-grey sheet covering the sky, through which the sun appears dimly.

results.name: Nimbostratus
results.description: Thick, dark, featureless layer producing continuous rain or snow.

results.name: Stratus
results.description: Uniform grey layer resembling fog that does not reach the ground; may drizzle.

results.name: Stratocumulus
results.description: Low, lumpy layer of grey or white rounded masses with gaps of clear sky.

results.name: Cumulus
results.description: Detached, puffy fair-weather clouds with flat bases and cauliflower tops.

results.name: Cumulonimbus
results.description: Towering thunderstorm cloud producing heavy rain, lightning, and hail.

results.name: Lenticular
results.description: Smooth, lens- or saucer-shaped clouds that form over hills and mountains.

results.name: Mammatus
results.description: Pouch-like bulges hanging beneath a cloud base, often after severe storms.

results.name: Contrail
results.description: Line-shaped ice clouds formed from aircraft engine exhaust at high altitude.
